title: Interference across the two/three boundary: one cancelling witness per knot
claim: Gadgets are sums over hidden bits of products of real functions of at most two variables. Theorem 1: with nonnegative values the support is the existential projection of the factor supports, hence majority-closed and never a knot, with any number of hidden bits. Theorem 2: with no hidden bits the support is never a knot, whatever the signs. Theorem 3: a clause of any width is 1 - prod(1 - literal), a signed gadget with one hidden bit, so a CNF with m clauses is a signed gadget with m hidden bits (the inclusion-exclusion identity both 2026 ETH refutations start from), and a relation excluding z tuples needs at most z. Theorem 4: each of the 16 classes of three-bit knots is exactly a signed gadget with one hidden bit and no fewer; the indicator has real tensor rank 2 for 14 classes (Cayley hyperdeterminant 1 for atoms, 4 for pairs at distance two and parity, 5 for three-excluded), while not-all-equal and twisted not-all-equal (hyperdeterminant -3, real rank 3) need one pairwise sign first; every decomposition has a negative entry, and the three-excluded and not-all-equal decompositions involve the golden ratio. Parity of n bits is one hidden bit with Hadamard edges.
failure_conditions: A nonnegative gadget of binary factors whose support is a knot.
A knot that is the support of a product of binary functions.
A three-bit knot class without an exact signed one-hidden-bit realization, or one with a signed zero-hidden-bit realization.
foundation_claim_scope: Set-level relations on bits; signed sums are a declared second reading of allowed states (a state is allowed when its signed witness sum is nonzero), tested beside the canonical existential reading, not a change to K1-K3.

validation.status: checked: 34 knots in 16 classes; 20,000 random nonnegative gadgets (support = projection, majority-closed, no knot); all 16^3 binary support triples (no knot); every clause of width 1-8 with all signs, 300 random 3-CNFs and all 256 three-bit relations against their one-bit-per-clause or per-excluded-tuple gadgets; exact sympy rank-2 decompositions for all 16 classes (two after a pairwise sign) verified symbolically on every input, each with a negative entry; parity of n <= 10 bits from one hidden bit; controls fire (perturbed decomposition, unscaled not-all-equal has no real rank-2 decomposition, absolute values enlarge every support, a 2-CNF relation is no knot); no human or external review
validation.novelty: Theorems 1-3 classical or elementary (Baker-Pixley, Schaefer; inclusion-exclusion; holographic transforms); Theorem 4 census: no overlap found (candidate local delta)
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-29.
